import re
src=open("preview.html",encoding="utf-8").read()

def balance(text, track):
    stack=[]; line=1; i=0; in_s=None; in_c=False; esc=False
    pairs={")":"(", "}":"{", "]":"["}
    while i<len(text):
        ch=text[i]
        if ch=="\n": line+=1
        if in_c:
            if ch=="\n": in_c=False
        elif in_s:
            if esc: esc=False
            elif ch=="\\": esc=True
            elif ch==in_s: in_s=None
        else:
            if ch in "\"'`": in_s=ch
            elif text[i:i+2]=="//": in_c=True; i+=2; continue
            elif text[i:i+2]=="/*":
                j=text.find("*/",i+2)
                if j<0: return "unterminated comment"
                line+=text[i:j].count("\n"); i=j+2; continue
            elif ch in "({[" and ch in track: stack.append((ch,line))
            elif ch in ")}]":
                if not stack: return f"extra {ch} at line {line}"
                o,l=stack.pop()
                if pairs[ch]!=o: return f"mismatch {o}@{l} vs {ch}@{line}"
        i+=1
    return stack or "balanced"

css=re.search(r"<style>(.*?)</style>",src,re.S).group(1)
js=re.search(r"<script>(.*?)</script>",src,re.S).group(1)

print("js brackets:", balance(js,"({["))

## What task 2 built (scientific mode) — reuse this, don't rebuild

### `window.FluxionMath` — the shared engine (task 3 and 4 should use it)

The script now has a clearly delimited engine section between
`ENGINE — FluxionMath` and `END ENGINE`, followed by the scientific-mode
controller IIFE. Everything lives in the same single inline classic script.
No `eval`, no `Function`: a hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser
(expression → term → unary → power → postfix → primary, right-associative `^`).

```js
FluxionMath.evaluate('sin(x)+1', { angle: 'deg', scope: { x: 30 } })
//   -> { ok: true,  value: 1.5, text: '1.5' }
//   -> { ok: false, error: 'a bracket has no value inside it', empty?: true }
FluxionMath.format(value)   // 12 sig figs, float noise trimmed, '1,234.5',

FluxionMath.pretty(src)     // display only: * -> ×, / -> ÷, - -> −,
                            // sqrt( -> √(, cbrt( -> ∛(, pi -> π, asin( -> sin⁻¹(
FluxionMath.constants        // {pi, tau, e, phi}
FluxionMath.functions        // ['sin','cos',...] names array
FluxionMath.significant      // 12
```

- `evaluate` never throws: malformed input comes back as `{ok:false, error}`.
  Unknown identifiers become an error unless they are in `scope` — so the graph
  mode just passes `{x: value}` per sample and `{angle: 'rad'}` (or `'deg'`).
- Supported: `+ - * / ^ %`, brackets `()[]{}`, unary ±, postfix `!`,
  implicit multiplication (`2pi`, `3(4+1)`, `(2)(3)`, `2sin(30)`),
  `%` = per cent when nothing follows / remainder between two values,
  digit grouping (`1 234`, `1,234`), `**` as `^`, `√`/`π`/`×`/`÷`/`−` glyphs.
  Functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan log ln log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil
  round sign. Constants: pi tau e phi. DEG/RAD applies to trig both ways.
  Domain errors (÷0, sqrt of negative, log ≤ 0, |asin|>1, tan 90°, 0^negative,
  non-integer factorial, overflow) return a readable message.

### Scientific panel DOM (all inside `#panel-scientific`, ids are stable)

`#sci-body.split--scientific` holds three grid children: `#sci-readout`
(`.readout--tall`: `#sci-expr`, `#sci-msg` (role=status, inline errors),
`#sci-value`, `.readout__foot` with the `deg`/`rad` `.seg` buttons `#sci-deg`
/`#sci-rad` and the `#sci-ans` chip, plus a `.sr-only` `#sci-announce`),
`.sci-console` (`#sci-keypad` 5-column keypad, 34 keys, `[data-ins]` /
`[data-act]`; `=` spans two columns) and `#sci-history`
(`#sci-history-list` of clickable restore buttons, `#sci-history-clear`).

mobile the DOM order is readout → keypad → history. Reuse unchanged.
